I'm on the Doha payroll (Qatar home country) and may work remotely from Bahrain (a permitted GCC host country) for up to 25 working days per calendar year. No single stay may exceed 14 calendar days, with a minimum 30-calendar-day gap between stays. The allowance resets on 01 January, is counted in home-country working days, and unused days lapse on 31 December. A partial working day in Bahrain counts as a full day; weekends and public holidays do not use the allowance but count toward the longest single stay. This is subject to case-by-case approval, eligibility criteria, tax/permanent establishment limits (no more than 60 calendar days total in Bahrain in a rolling 12-month period including leave and travel), and visa/entry rules.

My basic salary at the Doha branch is QAR 10,000 a month and I'm leaving after six and a half years. For Doha (Qatar), gratuity is 21 days of basic salary per year for years 1 to 5 and 28 days per year after year 5. The gratuity is paid in full on resignation once 1 year of service is complete. The daily wage for gratuity purposes is the monthly basic salary divided by 30. Years 1 to 5 give 5 x 21 = 105 days. The following 1.5 years give 1.5 x 28 = 42 days. The total is 147 days, and the gratuity is 147 x 10,000 / 30 = QAR 49,000.
